title: Why You Forget the Middle of Every List
hook: Always forgetting items in the middle of your shopping list?

narration.text: Your brain prioritises information at the start and end of any list.
This is known as the serial position effect.
The beginning items get more attention, moving into long term memory.
And the end items are still fresh in your short term memory.
The middle items lack these advantages, so they often get lost.
This effect applies to phone numbers, speeches, and even daily tasks.
Use this knowledge to structure information more effectively.
Have you noticed yourself forgetting the middle of things?

description: Ever wondered why you easily remember the beginning and end of a list but struggle with the middle? It is a common cognitive bias called the serial position effect. This video explains the memory science behind it.
topic: Why you often remember the beginning and end of a list better than the middle.
